Field.Help: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

The Credit Limit indicates the total amount allowed 'on account' in primary accounting currency. If the Credit Limit is 0, no check is performed. Credit Management is based on the Total Open Amount, which includes Vendor activities.

The Credit Used indicates the total amount of open or unpaid invoices in primary accounting currency for the Business Partner. Credit Management is based on the Total Open Amount, which includes Vendor activities.
The Acquisition Cost identifies the cost associated with making this prospect a customer.
The Potential Life Time Value is the anticipated revenue in primary accounting currency to be generated by the Business Partner.
Payment Terms identify the method and timing of payment.
The Actual Life Time Value is the recorded revenue in primary accounting currency generated by the Business Partner.
The Share indicates the percentage of this Business Partner's volume of the products supplied.
The Employee checkbox indicates if this Business Partner is an Employee. If it is selected, additional fields will display which further identify this employee.

Credit Management is inactive if Credit Status is No Credit Check, Credit Stop or if the Credit Limit is 0. If active, the status is set automatically set to Credit Hold, if the Total Open Balance is higher then the Credit Limit. It is set to Credit Watch, if above 90% of the Credit Limit and Credit OK otherwise.

Miminum Shelf Life of products with Guarantee Date instance. If > 0 you cannot select products with a shelf life ((Guarantee Date-Today) / Guarantee Days) less than the minum shelf life, unless you select "Show All"

The business partner is another organization in the system. So when performing transactions, the counter-document is created automatically. Example: You have BPartnerA linked to OrgA and BPartnerB linked to OrgB. If you create a sales order for BPartnerB in OrgA a purchase order is created for BPartnerA in OrgB. This allows to have explicit documents for Inter-Org transactions.

The Total Open Balance Amount is the calculated open item amount for Customer and Vendor activity. If the Balance is below zero, we owe the Business Partner. The amout is used for Credit Management. Invoices and Payment Allocations determine the Open Balance (i.e. not Orders or Payments).

Used for EDI and Credit Check - For details see http://www.dnb.com
Indicates the number of employees for this Business Partner. This field displays only for Prospects.

The NAICS/SIC identifies either of these codes that may be applicable to this Business Partner.
A summary entity represents a branch in a tree rather than an end-node. Summary entities are used for reporting and do not have own values.
The Language identifies the language to use for display and formatting
The Vendor checkbox indicates if this Business Partner is a Vendor. If it is selected, additional fields will display which further identify this vendor.
The Customer checkbox indicates if this Business Partner is a customer. If it is selected additional fields will display which further define this customer.
The Invoice Schedule identifies the frequency used when generating invoices.
The Prospect checkbox indicates an entity that is an active prospect.
The First Sale Date identifies the date of the first sale to this Business Partner

The Credit Limit indicates the total amount allowed 'on account' in primary accounting currency. If the Credit Limit is 0, no check is performed. Credit Management is based on the Total Open Amount, which includes Vendor activities.

The Credit Used indicates the total amount of open or unpaid invoices in primary accounting currency for the Business Partner. Credit Management is based on the Total Open Amount, which includes Vendor activities.
The Acquisition Cost identifies the cost associated with making this prospect a customer.
The Potential Life Time Value is the anticipated revenue in primary accounting currency to be generated by the Business Partner.
Payment Terms identify the method and timing of payment.
The Actual Life Time Value is the recorded revenue in primary accounting currency generated by the Business Partner.
The Share indicates the percentage of this Business Partner's volume of the products supplied.
The Employee checkbox indicates if this Business Partner is an Employee. If it is selected, additional fields will display which further identify this employee.
Company Agent is acting on behalf of the company with customers (Sales Representative, Customer Service, ...) or vendors (Purchasing Agent, ...). It could be an employee or external party.
Price Lists are used to determine the pricing, margin and cost of items purchased or sold.
Identifies the price list used by a Vendor for products purchased by this organization.
The URL defines an fully qualified web address like http://www.viennasolutions.com

If a business partner is exempt from tax, the exempt tax rate is used. For this, you need to set up a tax rate with a 0% rate and indicate that this is your tax exempt rate. This is required for tax reporting, so that you can track tax exempt transactions.
The Rating is used to differentiate the importance
The Payment Method indicates the method of invoice payment.
The Dunning indicates the rules and method of dunning for past due payments.
The Document Copies indicates the number of copies of each document that will be generated.
The Payment Rule indicates the method of purchase payment.
The partner's order reference is the order reference for this specific transaction.
The Greeting identifies the greeting to print on correspondence.
The Discount Printed Checkbox indicates if the discount will be printed on the document.
The Order Description identifies the standard description to use on orders for this Customer.
The Invoicing Rule defines how a Business Partner is invoiced and the frequency of invoicing.

The Shipping Rule indicates when an order should be delivered. For example should the order be delivered when the entire order is complete, when a line is complete or as the products become available.
Company Agent is acting on behalf of the company with customers (Sales Representative, Customer Service, ...) It could be an employee or external party.
The Freight Cost Rule indicates the method used when charging for freight.
The Shipping Method indicates how the products should be delivered. For example, will the order be picked up or shipped.
The Customer/Prospect Group provides a method of defining defaults to be used for individual Partners.
The PO Payment Term indicates the payment term that will be used when this purchase order becomes an invoice.
After calculation of the (standard) price, the trade discount percentage is calculated and applied resulting in the final price.
Send emails with document attached (e.g. Invoice, Delivery Note, etc.)
The parent (organization) of the Business Partner for reporting purposes.

Credit Management is inactive if Credit Status is No Credit Check, Credit Stop or if the Credit Limit is 0. If active, the status is set automatically set to Credit Hold, if the Total Open Balance is higher then the Credit Limit. It is set to Credit Watch, if above 90% of the Credit Limit and Credit OK otherwise.

Miminum Shelf Life of products with Guarantee Date instance. If > 0 you cannot select products with a shelf life ((Guarantee Date-Today) / Guarantee Days) less than the minum shelf life, unless you select "Show All"

The business partner is another organization in the system. So when performing transactions, the counter-document is created automatically. Example: You have BPartnerA linked to OrgA and BPartnerB linked to OrgB. If you create a sales order for BPartnerB in OrgA a purchase order is created for BPartnerA in OrgB. This allows to have explicit documents for Inter-Org transactions.

The Total Open Balance Amount is the calculated open item amount for Customer and Vendor activity. If the Balance is below zero, we owe the Business Partner. The amout is used for Credit Management. Invoices and Payment Allocations determine the Open Balance (i.e. not Orders or Payments).
Size category of the Business Partner; Examples could be Number of Employees, Revenue, Number Outlets/Stores, etc.
User defined status of the Business Partner. This could be used for lead tracking in addition to lead management functionality in Requests.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. The business partner is another organization in the system. So when performing transactions, the counter-document is created automatically. Example: You have BPartnerA linked to OrgA and BPartnerB linked to OrgB. If you create a sales order for BPartnerB in OrgA a purchase order is created for BPartnerA in OrgB. This allows to have explicit documents for Inter-Org transactions.

Credit Management is inactive if Credit Status is No Credit Check, Credit Stop or if the Credit Limit is 0. If active, the status is set automatically set to Credit Hold, if the Total Open Balance is higher then the Credit Limit. It is set to Credit Watch, if above 90% of the Credit Limit and Credit OK otherwise.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

The Total Open Balance Amount is the calculated open item amount for Customer and Vendor activity. If the Balance is below zero, we owe the Business Partner. The amout is used for Credit Management. Invoices and Payment Allocations determine the Open Balance (i.e. not Orders or Payments).

The business partner is another organization in the system. So when performing transactions, the counter-document is created automatically. Example: You have BPartnerA linked to OrgA and BPartnerB linked to OrgB. If you create a sales order for BPartnerB in OrgA a purchase order is created for BPartnerA in OrgB. This allows to have explicit documents for Inter-Org transactions.

So, @Name@ would resolve into the User name (if user is defined defined), then Account name (if Account is defined) and then the Name of the business object if it has a Name.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.
The Comments field allows for free form entry of additional information.
